meta.note: Statuses are set by hand in the workbook. The numeric bands behind each status are published under "thresholds"; in-range carries no color indicator, by design. Palma North/South are in lease-up and four of their KPIs are scored against the lease-up overrides. A cell carries a colour and counts toward the tally only where a report has supplied a number and the published band could grade it; the workbook's hand-set symbol is kept in "statuses" and in "status_workbook" but is not treated as a result. Measured values, where present, are computed from the underlying report and their status is derived from the published band rather than set by hand.

Leased %.how: (Occupied + vacant-rented + notice-rented) / total units, at month-end
Leased %.basis: Band set by Kaelin, July 2026, superseding the data-derived range. Deliberately aggressive: The Landing's T12 economic occupancy of ~97.7% (vacancy loss $377,834 on $16.49M GPR) scores amber against a 99% green, and SF metro vacancy of ~4.6% implies a market-average asset lands amber as well.

Trade-out %.how: (New effective rent − prior effective rent, same unit) / prior rent. Blend new + renewal, trailing 3 months
Trade-out %.basis: SF multifamily rent growth ran ~5.7–5.9% YoY through Q4 2025 (market sourcing per the Expense Benchmark workbook). Green requires capturing at least market growth, not just avoiding a rollback.

Concession Load %.how: Total concessions granted / gross potential rent, trailing 3 months
Concession Load %.basis: The Landing T12 concessions were $10,672 on $16.49M GPR = 0.06% — effectively zero. Palma North carries $39,905 of recurring concessions incl. one unit at 3 months free. Stabilized assets here should sit near zero; see lease-up overrides below.

Loss to Lease %.how: (Market rent − in-place rent) / market rent, current rent roll
Loss to Lease %.basis: The Landing T12 loss-to-lease was $2,629,358 on $16,489,513 market rent potential = 15.9%, which scores red against this band. Before wiring it, confirm Yardi 'Market rent potential' is set to true achievable market rent — if it is aspirational, every property will read artificially high.

NOI Margin %.how: NOI / total revenue, T12 accrual basis (GL 5999-9999 / 4999-9999)
NOI Margin %.basis: Band set by Kaelin, July 2026, superseding the data-derived range. Aggressive relative to current performance: The Landing T12 NOI of $9,354,210 on revenue $14,077,351 = 66.4%, which now scores amber. Typical stabilized multifamily runs 55–62%, so the red line sits at the top of the national norm — justified by this portfolio's Prop 13 tax basis and low utility load ($745/unit vs. $1,870 SF benchmark).

Budget Variance %.how: ABS( (actual controllable opex − budget) / budget ), YTD — absolute magnitude, direction ignored
Budget Variance %.basis: Band set by Kaelin, July 2026. Scored on absolute magnitude, so a 12% underspend flags red exactly like a 12% overrun — correct, because a large favorable variance is usually timing lag or deferred maintenance rather than outperformance. This removes the need for two-sided handling on this KPI. Boundary: the ≤/> classifier puts exactly 5.0% in green and exactly 10.0% in amber; only matters at the precise boundary.

Controllable OpEx/Unit.how: Controllable opex (utilities, contract services, R&M, payroll, G&A, marketing, turnover) / unit count, T12 annualized. Excludes taxes, insurance, management fee
Controllable OpEx/Unit.basis: The Landing T12 actual = $7,784/unit ($649/mo) across 263 units. Sum of the SF-adjusted category benchmarks = $8,050/unit. Band brackets both, so the current actual scores in-range.

# of Tours/Leads/Applications.how: Tours / available units, per month. NORMALIZE — raw counts are not comparable across a 263-unit and a 46-unit asset
# of Tours/Leads/Applications.basis: Palma North logged 28 shows over 05/01–07/14/26 against 22 available units ≈ 0.6/unit/mo; Palma South logged 21. The raw counts on the current scorecard cannot be compared property to property — normalizing is the fix.

Closing Ratio.basis: Palma South: 4 applications on 21 shows = 19.0% applied, 3 approved = 14.3%. Industry stabilized norm is 25–35%; luxury urban product runs at the low end of that.

# of Renewals.how: Renewals signed / lease expirations in the period (renewal conversion rate)
# of Renewals.basis: Normalized from a raw count. 50–60% is the typical stabilized range. Always read alongside % Increase so retention isn't being bought with flat renewals.

# of offers that are 30 days.how: Renewal offers issued ≥ 30 days before expiration / total upcoming expirations (on-time issuance rate)
# of offers that are 30 days.basis: DEFINITION AMBIGUOUS on the current sheet. Read the other way — offers left outstanding 30+ days — lower is better and the band flips to green ≤ 5%, amber 5–15%, red > 15%. Confirm intent before wiring.

# of accepted/pending offers.how: Accepted offers / offers issued, trailing 3 months. Track 'pending' separately as an aging, not as a score
# of accepted/pending offers.basis: Follows from the 60% renewal-conversion green: acceptance rate should sit slightly below conversion once non-responses are netted out.

# of month to month.how: MTM leases / occupied units, at month-end
# of month to month.basis: The Landing earned $68,774 of MTM fee income in T12 — MTM is revenue-positive short term but a forecasting and turnover risk. Palma North reported 0 MTM leases at 07/14/26.

% Increase.how: Average renewal rent increase %, trailing 3 months
% Increase.basis: TWO-SIDED: above +7% the green flips to amber, because aggressive renewals push turnover and re-lease cost that exceeds the rent gain. Anchored to SF rent growth of ~5.7–5.9% YoY.

Total Deliquency.how: Total gross resident AR balance / one month's billed rent, at month-end
Total Deliquency.basis: The Landing T12 net bad debt was $100,867 on $14.08M revenue = 0.7%. Score on GROSS AR: Palma North's rent roll nets to a −$84,450 credit balance because of two large prepaid accounts, which would hide real delinquency behind a negative total.

Split Between 30/60/90.how: Share of total AR aged 60+ days
Split Between 30/60/90.basis: A distribution cannot be scored as a single value. Collapsing it to the 60+ share keeps the signal that matters (older AR is materially less collectible) while still fitting the three-band key.

POs over 30 days.how: Open POs aged > 30 days / total open POs
POs over 30 days.basis: Suggested operating standard — no portfolio history for this metric exists in the source files. Recalibrate after one quarter of actuals.

# of invoices processed.how: Invoices approved within 5 business days / invoices received
# of invoices processed.basis: Reframed from a raw count to a cycle-time rate. A high invoice count is neither good nor bad on its own — it measures workload, not performance.

# of work orders.how: Count of work orders still open in the queue at time of reporting (point-in-time backlog, not volume opened)
# of work orders.basis: Band set by Kaelin, July 2026. Measures backlog rather than volume, so an absolute count holds across asset sizes — a clean queue is a clean queue at 263 units or 46. Boundary note: 10 fell in both the amber and red bands as specified and is scored red, making amber 5–9. Cutoffs are integers (green ≤ 4 = under 5; red > 9 = 10 or more).

Work orders over two days.how: Count of open work orders aged more than 48 hours, at time of reporting
Work orders over two days.basis: Band set by Kaelin, July 2026. Zero-tolerance green — a single ticket past 48 hours moves the property off green. NOTE: this KPI exists on 'KPI (Flipped Axis)' but is missing from 'Nicholas MVP' — the two tabs carry 20 and 19 KPIs respectively.

Online Review Rating.how: Average Google / ILS star rating, trailing 90 days
Online Review Rating.basis: PROPOSED — no portfolio history in the source files. 4.5+ is the practical threshold at which rating stops suppressing ILS conversion; below 4.0 it actively costs tours.

Review Response Rate.how: Reviews responded to within 5 business days / total reviews received
Review Response Rate.basis: PROPOSED. Response rate is fully within onsite control, unlike the rating itself, so the green bar is set high deliberately.

Resident Satisfaction (CSAT).how: Satisfied + very satisfied responses / total responses, annual resident survey
Resident Satisfaction (CSAT).basis: PROPOSED. Report alongside response count — a 90% CSAT on 8 responses at a 263-unit asset is not a signal. Suppress the rating below ~30 responses.

Maintenance Satisfaction.how: Satisfied responses / completed work-order surveys returned, trailing 90 days
Maintenance Satisfaction.basis: PROPOSED. Pairs with the two maintenance KPIs: closing tickets fast at low satisfaction means work is being marked complete before it is.

Open Elise Tasks.how: Count of unresolved tasks in the EliseAI queue at time of reporting
Open Elise Tasks.basis: PROPOSED, mirroring the open work order band set 07/2026 — both are point-in-time queue backlogs, so holding one convention across them keeps the scorecard readable. Integer cutoffs (green ≤ 4; red > 9).

Elise Tasks over 24 Hours.how: Count of open EliseAI tasks aged more than 24 hours
Elise Tasks over 24 Hours.basis: PROPOSED, mirroring the 'Work orders over two days' band. Tighter clock than maintenance (24h vs 48h) because these are mostly prospect and resident replies, where response speed drives conversion.

AI Containment Rate.how: Prospect conversations resolved by EliseAI with no human handoff / total conversations
AI Containment Rate.basis: PROPOSED. Read against Closing Ratio, not alone — high containment with a falling close rate means the AI is deflecting leads rather than converting them.

Avg First Response Time.how: Mean minutes from new prospect inquiry to first reply (AI or human)
Avg First Response Time.basis: PROPOSED. Minutes, not hours — an AI leasing assistant should make this near-instant, so a reading above 15 minutes usually indicates a routing or integration failure rather than slow staff.

leaseup_overrides.approach: Widen — concessions are the lease-up tool
Score vs. lease-up pro forma NOI, not a margin %
Score vs. budget, not the per-unit benchmark
